To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Dirac- Brueckner approach is applicable to the description of nuclear matter at high density, but the angle-averaging of the nucleon momentum squared is not valid.

the equation of state of asymmetric nuclear matter and the nucleon self-energy are well approximated by the angle-averaged and momentum-averaged ones, respectively, and that the parametrizations for both the equation of state and the nucleon single-particle potential are accurate up to densities of 1.5-2.0 times nuclear-matter saturation density.

(i) the angle-averaged approach is valid up to densities of about 0.6 fm-3, (ii) the momentum-averaged approach can be safely applied up to 0.8-0.9 fm-3, and (iii) the nucleon self-energy can be accurately described by polynomials of the nucleon momentum up to about 0.8 fm-3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the equation of state of asymmetric nuclear matter and its implications to the structure of neutron stars.
the following topics: 1) the equation of state of dense nuclear matter, 2) the neutron star structure, 3) the nuclear matter incompressibility and 4) the nuclear symmetry energy.
a systematic study of the equation of state and nucleon self- energies in nuclear matter, and their application to neutron stars.

our results are consistent with the previous results of the Dirac- Brueckner-H artree-Fock approach and the results of the variational method.
the Dirac- Brueckner approach with the Bonn potentials provides a reasonable description of the properties of dense matter in neutron stars.
, within the Dirac- Brueckner-HF approximation, the angle-averaged approach is valid for symmetric nuclear matter at densities below about 0.6 nucleons/fm3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, within the present framework, the equation of state of dense nuclear matter is reasonably determined up to the density of about 2-3 times the normal nuclear density.
the Dirac- Brueckner-HF approach is a reliable method to investigate nuclear matter properties and neutron stars.

the Dirac- Brueckner-HF theory can be used to describe the properties of dense matter up to densities around 2-3 times the normal nuclear matter density, and that it is a reliable tool to study the properties of dense asymmetric nuclear matter and neutron stars.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a proper treatment of the momentum averaging is essential in obtaining reliable results for the nucleon self-energy in dense nuclear matter.

the Dirac- Brueckner-HF approach is applicable to dense, asymmetric nuclear matters, and that the angle-averaged and momentum-averaged approximations are valid up to high densities, at least for the Bonn potentials.
, for a wide class of the Bonn potentials and for the densities relevant to neutron stars, the angle-averaged self-energies are very close to those calculated without any approximation.
